LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING - FICTIONAL AND NON-FICTIONAL

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we relate events in a text with real life, people or places? 2. How can we predict what will happen in a text or story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading - Fictional and Non-fictional together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to be self-driven and perform tasks on their own is enhanced as they engage in self- driven tasks by inferring the meaning of unfamiliar words and phrases.

 Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s ability to – The learner comes up with unique and new ideas through creation of

mind maps using words in a text.

Values:
